plain: To twist the meaning of facts or words so they are no longer true

webster.text: To twist out of natural or regular shape; as, to distort the neck, the limbs or the body; to distort the features.

more.text: To wrest from the true meaning; to pervert; as, to distort passages of scripture, or their meaning.

example.quote: Under these circumstances, how easy would it be for an ambitious, factious demagogue to misrepresent him, to distort the features of his character, and give a false color to his conduct !
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 23, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
